fact: Access Now's #KeepItOn report on 2025 lists a shutdown in the DRC at Goma, in the M23 conflict area, among the year's recorded shutdowns; the document does not say who ordered it, when in 2025 it began or whether it ended.

fact: The Committee to Protect Journalists says journalist Tresor Muntu was detained on 15 September 2026 and charged with defamation and publishing false news for sharing a post criticising a provincial politician, and jailed on 16 September.

LINAPYCO's Fidele Mbilizi Mutimanwa criticised the DRC state's non-implementation of the African Commission's 2022 Batwa decision and of national law 22/030, and park clearance operations, at an ACHPR89 side event; the article gives no event date, so its published date is used.

OLPA reports that journalist Tresor Muntu was arrested on 15 September 2026 and prosecuted for defaming a provincial assembly vice-president over a WhatsApp-shared post accusing her of using influence in a land dispute, and was released on 18 September.

OLPA reports that two Radio Ndenga News technicians in Kalemie were detained by people presenting as ANR agents from 14 to 16 September 2026 after refusing to stop the rebroadcast of a programme on protests against the constitutional change project.

OLPA reports that journalist Michael Tenende was held by the ANR from 30 August to 8 September 2026 over a social media message calling for a boycott of the Lomami governor's rally, which he denied writing.
OLPA says the main mobile phone networks in Fizi have been cut since July 2026; the source names no order for it.
ISS Africa lists the Democratic Republic of the Congo among six Central African countries with an internet shutdown recorded in 2025.
Access Now says the Democratic Republic of the Congo shut down the internet across Goma throughout a humanitarian crisis in 2025.
Global Voices says Fizi territory in South Kivu was offline for over a month from July 2026; the source gives no order.
